correctness.rationale: For all existing finite affine planes of order q>=3, the exact distance classes and the no-2-points-plus-2-lines clique rule give K=U union V. Relative cone collapses prove U contractible and V equivalent to the join B of q+1 discrete q-point parallel classes; U intersect V is exactly the incidence graph G. Since B is (q-1)^(q+1) wedges of S^q it is simply connected, so G->B is null and K is B wedge suspension(G). The connected graph cycle rank E-V+1=(q-1)^2(q+1), giving the two claimed sphere counts integrally. A point is a universal vertex in the scale-three graph power, so there is no homology beyond threshold 3. The standalone finite verifier exhausts q=3 and confirms beta_2=beta_3=16; q=2 regression has beta_2=4. No finite enumeration is used as an all-q proof.

value.rationale: The affine-plane Levi graphs are a canonical family of highly constrained incidence structures, and their distance-two graph powers have a natural topological gap not determined by graph rank or generic bipartite-square theorems. The all-order formula explains a mixed-dimensional wedge by the join of parallel classes and computes complete positive-dimensional graph-metric persistence at every scale, with a first substantive 21-vertex Hesse example (16 S2 and 16 S3). This is a motivated structural result for all existing affine planes, including non-Desarguesian ones, not an arbitrary tiny finite table or straightforward renaming of the projective-plane theorem.
